Subsidy is 15% urban / 25% rural for the general category, and 25% urban / 35% rural for special categories. Own contribution is 10% general and 5% special. For MSE loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, including PMEGP units, banks must lend without collateral up to ₹20 lakh under RBI's Lending to MSME Sector (Amendment) Directions, 2026 (RBI/2025-26/206, 9 February 2026). Banks may go up to ₹25 lakh without collateral based on track record. Apply at pmegp.msme.gov.in.

Subsidy is 15% urban / 25% rural for the general category, and 25% urban / 35% rural for special categories. Own contribution is 10% general and 5% special. For MSE loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, including PMEGP units, banks must lend without collateral up to ₹20 lakh under RBI's Lending to MSME Sector (Amendment) Directions, 2026 (RBI/2025-26/206, 9 February 2026). Banks may go up to ₹25 lakh without collateral based on track record. Apply at pmegp.msme.gov.in.

old claim: For registered traditional artisans (potters, toy makers, tailors and other listed trades): skill training with a stipend, a ₹15,000 toolkit incentive and collateral-free loans at 5% interest.

Coverage is generally 75% (higher for micro enterprises, women, SC/ST and the North East). For MSE loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, including PMEGP units, banks must lend without collateral up to ₹20 lakh under RBI/2025-26/206. Banks may go up to ₹25 lakh without collateral based on track record.

old claim: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy, up to ₹10 lakh per unit, for micro food-processing businesses. ODOP products get priority.
new text: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy, capped at ₹10 lakh per individual micro food-processing unit. Confirmed by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries only until 30 September 2026. Apply via pmfme.mofpi.gov.in.

old claim: A government credit guarantee that lets banks lend to micro and small enterprises without collateral. Ask your bank for a CGTMSE-covered loan.

old claim: Credit-linked subsidy for new units: projects up to ₹50 lakh (manufacturing) or ₹20 lakh (services), with 15–35% of project cost as subsidy depending on your category and whether you are in a rural area.

Coverage is generally 75% (higher for micro enterprises, women, SC/ST and the North East). For MSE loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, including PMEGP units, banks must lend without collateral up to ₹20 lakh under RBI/2025-26/206. Banks may go up to ₹25 lakh without collateral based on track record.

old claim: Credit-linked subsidy for new units: projects up to ₹50 lakh (manufacturing) or ₹20 lakh (services), with 15–35% of project cost as subsidy depending on your category and whether you are in a rural area.
new text: New units under the December 2023 guidelines (approved through 2025-26): project cost up to ₹50 lakh for manufacturing or ₹20 lakh for service. Subsidy is 15% urban / 25% rural for the general category, and 25% urban / 35% rural for special categories. Own contribution is 10% general and 5% special. For MSE loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026, including PMEGP units, banks must lend without collateral up to ₹20 lakh under RBI's Lending to MSME Sector (Amendment) Directions, 2026 (RBI/2025-26/206, 9 February 2026). Banks may go up to ₹25 lakh without collateral based on track record. Apply at pmegp.msme.gov.in.
